stages.title: Trade, competitiveness, FDI and fiscal policy
stages.sub: After this you can explain the trade balance, what drives competitiveness, why FDI matters, how tax changes affect it, and what discretionary fiscal policy means.

steps.q: A country sells £300bn of goods and services abroad and buys £340bn from abroad in a year. Has it earned more from exports than it spent on imports?
steps.right: No, it has spent more than it earned
steps.wrong: Yes, it has earned more than it spent
steps.hint: Compare the two numbers: exports versus imports.

steps.q: Two countries make similar cars, but one country's cars are cheaper, better made, and delivered faster. Which country's firms will buyers choose?
steps.right: The one with cheaper, better, faster cars
steps.hint: Think about what actually makes a buyer pick one seller over another: price and quality matter, not size.

steps.q: A German car firm builds and runs its own factory in the UK, employing UK workers and controlling operations there, rather than just buying shares in a UK firm.
steps.right: It has built lasting productive capacity it controls abroad
steps.wrong: It has made a short-term trade in UK shares
steps.hint: Notice it built and runs a factory itself, rather than just holding paper assets.

steps.q: A government cuts corporation tax sharply, so firms keep more of their profits after tax. Would foreign firms find it more or less attractive to build factories there now?
steps.right: More attractive, more firms may invest
steps.wrong: Less attractive, fewer firms will invest
steps.hint: Lower tax on profit means a firm keeps more of what it earns from investing there.

steps.q: Facing a downturn, a government deliberately announces a new one-off round of tax cuts and extra spending this year, rather than letting existing tax and benefit rules respond automatically. Is this a deliberate, chosen change, or one that happens automatically as the economy moves?
steps.wrong: An automatic change with no decision needed
steps.hint: The government is announcing and deciding on it this year, not just letting existing rules run.
